current.text: He is a first-round rookie, age 19.
He is the backup point guard behind CJ McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Atlanta expects a 10-man rotation with him on the bench.
Lloyd expects him to struggle with usage and efficiency as a rookie, but to be a good source of assists and steals.
ESPN's rank of 215 is too high for him this season.

He would likely start if McCollum got hurt, but the path is not clean. Several Atlanta starters handle the ball, and Lu Dort or Andrew Wiggins could replace any of them, so he is not an automatic handcuff.
Atlanta has no true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels share the ball handling.
In Summer League he scored 9 points and ran the offense, with 7 assists, a 4.1 to 1 assist to turnover ratio, 1.5 steals and 1.3 blocks.
Atlanta plays 4-4-3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not a concern.

durable.text: His fantasy appeal comes from his assist to turnover ratio and his steal rate. Experts rank him ahead of Mikel Brown Jr. for fantasy for those reasons.
One expert says his wingspan is not great.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD and rank him 243 (Yahoo) and 215 (ESPN). Our draft takes only 144 players and he was not drafted last season, so do not draft him. His projected line (about 10 points, 3.8 assists, 1.1 steals, few threes) has no strong category, so he fits no particular build. Watch him on waivers. He becomes worth an add only if CJ McCollum misses time and Flemings, not Lu Dort or Andrew Wiggins, takes the starting minutes and turns them into assists and steals.
